identity.title: Scaling Laws and Spectra of Shallow Neural Networks in the Feature Learning Regime

problem.claim: The paper analyzes scaling laws and weight-spectrum behavior for shallow quadratic and diagonal neural networks in the feature-learning regime.

gap.claim: The authors identify that theoretical understanding of neural scaling laws remains largely confined to linear models.

contributions.claim: A systematic analysis of scaling laws for quadratic and diagonal neural networks in the feature-learning regime.
A detailed phase diagram for excess-risk scaling exponents as functions of sample complexity and weight decay, using connections to matrix compressed sensing and LASSO.
A detailed characterization linking scaling regimes to the spectral properties of trained network weights.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a first-principles theoretical interpretation connecting power-law tails in weight spectra with network generalization performance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The analysis reveals crossovers between distinct scaling regimes and plateau behavior, phenomena the authors say mirror reports from empirical neural-scaling research.
The authors establish a precise link between the identified regimes and spectral properties of trained weights.
The authors report theoretical validation of empirical observations associating power-law tails in weight spectra with generalization performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Neural scaling laws have driven advances in deep learning, but their theory is described as largely limited to linear models.
The paper studies quadratic and diagonal networks in feature learning and derives excess-risk scaling exponents across sample complexity and weight decay.
It identifies regime crossovers and plateaus, then relates them to trained-weight spectra and power-law tails associated with generalization.

source_observation.claim: The abstract organizes scaling behavior through a phase diagram indexed by sample complexity and weight decay, then connects those regimes to weight spectra and generalization.

lessons.interpretation: This framing makes regime-dependent behavior and its proposed mechanism easier to state together.
lessons.application: For a theory paper on scaling, define the control variables and regime map before presenting spectral or performance interpretations.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the phenomenon has no meaningful regime boundaries or when the proposed spectral link is not established by the available analysis.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical scaling exponents, phase boundaries, model dimensions, data assumptions, or training details.
The abstract does not specify the exact sense or conditions of the reported theoretical validation and precise spectral link.
